column3: Exact repetition of the focus description of every lying, sinful recipient.
Abandoning received signs and being pursued by Satan gives a related path into satanic misguidance.
False speech about God and the question of how people are turned away develop the focus's lying and inversion.
It identifies the denier as a transgressing sinner, closely matching the focus's recipient type.
The immediate preceding question introduces those upon whom the devils descend.
Its language of being turned away supplies a direct but less specific counterpart to falsehood.
The obstructer of good is characterized as transgressing and sinful, a related moral profile.
Satanic fear-making is a broad hostile influence without the focus's false transmission.
Changing a heard command incurs sin before the all-hearing, all-knowing God, linking false handling to culpability.
Angelic descent by the Lord's permission is a distant contrast to the devils' descent.
The immediate continuation says the recipients relay what they hear and that most are liars.
The absence of sinful speech in Paradise does not clarify satanic descent or its recipients.
God's rejection of every ungrateful sinner supplies a related judgment on the focus's sinful type.
Righteous deeds and their reward provide only a general contrast to habitual sin.
Bearing sin and receiving punishment is a broad consequence rather than a transmission parallel.
Return to God and His power do not illuminate the lying recipients or descent.
Seeking refuge from Satan when reciting the Quran forms a relevant protective contrast to satanic communication.
The absence of sinful speech around Paradise's drink is only lexical overlap.
Universal creation and guardianship add no specific link to satanic descent.
Devils performing work under divine guard provide a related scene of restrained satanic agents.
The rebuke of choosing false gods directly develops falsehood directed against God.
A revealed surah exposes what hypocrites hide, contrasting disclosure with the focus's deceptive recipients.
Satan's attempted insertion into prophetic recitation is the direct counter-model to authentic revelation.
Prideful persistence in sin supplies only a general trait of a sinful person.
An audience demands a heavenly book, while the messenger limits his role, paralleling contested descent and revelation.
People acknowledge their Creator yet are turned away, a concise counterpart to being deluded by falsehood.
Fabricating falsehood while worshipping idols directly joins lying with satanically opposed worship.
The demand to produce the Torah addresses disputed claims but not satanic descent.
Following Satan leads to indecency and evil, supplying the moral mechanism behind sinful conduct.
The pilgrimage timing instruction and its exemption from sin add no relevant transmission link.
It explicitly marks their speech as issuing from falsehood, closely matching the focus's lying recipients.
Bound captives do not clarify the focus apart from a remote satanic context.
Illicitly taking wealth through sin is a concrete but unrelated instance of wrongdoing.
The slanderous falsehood and each person's earned sin connect deception with moral liability.
Joseph names Satan's disruption of family relations, a limited example of satanic incitement.
False accusation and manifest sin connect harmful lying with culpability.
It forbids sin, transgression, association, and speaking about God without knowledge, closely framing false religious speech.
Satan beautifies people's deeds and then abandons them, showing deceptive satanic influence in action.
God knows what people do, giving direct divine awareness of the deeds that mark the focus's recipients.
After affirming God as Creator, it asks how people are turned away, echoing the focus's false inversion.
The mention of devils as workers provides a related but nonspecific satanic-agent setting.
The arrival of Pharaoh and earlier peoples with wrongdoing gives only a general culpability parallel.
The fate of an obstinate disbeliever is a general judgment without the focus's deception motif.
The wind subjected to Solomon has no material connection to the focus.
Correcting a bequest involving sin does not clarify satanic descent.
The gathering of skilled magicians is only a broad local contrast with deceptive supernatural claims.
Turning from the Merciful's reminder results in an attached devil, a related account of satanic accompaniment.
Disbelievers call the message an old falsehood, directly portraying a false response to revelation.
The warning against a habitual slanderer is a limited ethical parallel to lying.
The regret over an evil companion does not explain the focus's descent or recipient type.
The naming of major sin in intoxicants and gambling gives a concrete moral contrast to the sinful recipient.
The food of the sinful person adds only the label and a punishment setting.
It commands leaving open and hidden sin and promises recompense for what sinners earn.
The call for skilled magicians is only a remote contrast to satanic communication.
Moses' sign consumes the false fabrication of the magicians, opposing deceptive claims.
The harsh, base character sketch offers little beyond a broad corrupt profile.
Hypocritical speech that sounds persuasive yet conceals enmity gives a relevant example of deceptive utterance.
The slanderer who carries tales supplies only a limited lying-speech parallel.
The failure of falsely invented gods exposes both fabrication and misplaced devotion.
Hostile demands for a treasure or angel pressure the messenger, paralleling contested revelation and transmission.
Taking property through false accusation and manifest sin is a specific but distant wrongdoing.
God's dominion and power do not clarify the focus's recipient or descent.
Disbelievers demand a sign while the prophet is only a warner, a related scene of resisting divine communication.
God's reckoning of all things provides only a broad accountability frame.
Universal mortality does not add to the focus.
A sending-down from the Merciful supplies a direct divine contrast to the focus's satanic descent.
Replacement of a sign and divine power do not develop lying recipients.
God's control of dominion is too general for the focus's deceptive transmission.
Gathering all people and divine power provide only broad eschatological background.
God as witness over everything supplies a general accountability counterpart to hidden deception.
God knows what is concealed and disclosed, directly countering the hidden falsehood of the recipients.
The demand for a book from heaven and the people's wrongdoing form a related rejection-of-revelation scene.
The messenger as witness over his community supports accountable reception of communicated revelation.
Attributing calamity to people's own actions is only a broad responsibility theme.
Abraham's request concerning resurrection does not clarify the focus.
Witnesses from every community provide an accountability setting for people's response to messages.
The shares from good or evil intercession are only an indirect consequence-of-action parallel.
The parable of lightning and blindness does not add a clear link to the focus.
Provision for Israel and their self-wronging do not clarify satanic descent.
The parable of worldly life has no material connection to the focus.
God accounts for what people reveal or conceal, directly opposing the secrecy of false and sinful conduct.
The distribution of spoils and divine power do not illuminate the focus.
Hostile wish to turn believers back, followed by awaiting God's command, gives a related opposition-to-faith setting.
Those with deviation pursue ambiguity while God alone knows its interpretation, a relevant contrast to false handling of revelation.
Legal conduct is closed by God's comprehensive knowledge, broadly placing actions under divine awareness.
The revival sign demonstrates divine power but not the focus's deception or descent.
God knows what is within breasts while people conceal their claims, directly exposing hidden inward falsehood.
The sending of winds and rain does not clarify the focus.
Even extraordinary signs would not make many disbelievers believe, a relevant limit on resistance to revelation.
Belief in God's angels, books, and messengers provides a broad authentic-revelation contrast.
The threatened marking of the condemned man supplies a nearby judgment context for the corrupt profile in this passage.
The description of couches in Paradise has no connection to the focus.
The blessed Book and call to follow it provide only a broad authentic-scripture contrast.
Punishment for wrongdoing is a general consequence without a transmission link.
The household access instruction does not add to the focus.
The detailed legal instruction concludes with God's comprehensive knowledge, giving a broad contrast to dishonest dealing.
Repentance and forgiveness do not clarify the focus's lying or satanic descent.
God knows believers' hidden self-betrayal, directly linking divine knowledge with concealed wrongdoing.
Noah is forbidden to ask without knowledge and his son's deed is called unrighteous, paralleling bounded knowledge and moral evaluation.
The testing of the garden owners begins a general account of wrongful intent and consequence.
The revelation is sent down by the Lord of the worlds, the central divine contrast to satanic descent.
The trustworthy Spirit brings the revelation down, directly opposing the devils' descent in the focus.
The descent reaches the prophet's heart so that he may warn, clarifying the authentic recipient and purpose.
Its clear Arabic delivery continues the account of authentic revelation against counterfeit transmission.
It explicitly denies that the devils brought the Quran down, making the focus's demonic descent a decisive contrast.
The devils are neither suited nor able to bring this message, delimiting their role.
The devils are barred from hearing, directly opposing any claim that they receive the revealed message.
The warning against invoking another god gives the immediate religious boundary around the counterfeit-transmission passage.
The messenger declares himself free from what the disobedient do, closely paralleling the focus's sinful recipients.
Reliance on the Mighty, Merciful One supplies the prophet's response within the same warning sequence.
God sees the prophet when he stands, supporting divine oversight of the messenger in this immediate context.
God sees his movements among those who prostrate, continuing the contrast with concealed demonic activity.
God is the Hearing, Knowing One, directly grounding knowledge of speech and hidden reception in the passage.
The misguided follow the poets, opening the passage's counterpart to the lying recipients of satanic communication.
The poets' wandering in every valley depicts ungrounded, erratic speech after the focus's counterfeit transmission.
They say what they do not do, directly developing false speech joined to moral failure.
The believing poets who do righteous deeds mark the exception to the preceding false and wayward speech.
It explicitly says the Quran is not the speech of an accursed devil, a direct doctrinal counterpart to the focus.
Devils teach people magic and are identified with disbelief, directly linking devils, corrupt communication, and sin.
Human and jinn devils inspire one another with embellished false speech, closely paralleling satanic transmission to deceptive people.
Hearts incline to that false speech, and its hearers earn what they earn, joining reception, falsehood, and sin.
Devils inspire their allies to dispute, a direct example of demonic communication entering human speech.
The heaven is guarded from every accursed devil, supplying a cosmological boundary on satanic access.
A devil who snatches a hearing is pursued by a clear flame, directly delimiting stolen communication.
The heaven is guarded from every rebellious devil, reinforcing exclusion from authentic heavenly communication.
They cannot listen to the highest assembly and are driven away, closely clarifying the focus's devils.
They are repelled and face lasting punishment, completing the denial of their heavenly access.
The jinn find heaven filled with strong guards and flames, a related account of blocked access.
Those seeking to listen now find a flame lying in wait, directly paralleling forbidden hearing.
Satan has no authority over those who believe and rely on their Lord, contrasting faithful reception with the focus's recipients.
His authority is limited to those who take him as patron and associate others with God, defining the susceptible recipients.
Satan disavows coercive authority and admits only calling people, distinguishing invitation from divine revelation.
Devils are sent against disbelievers to incite them, a related mode of satanic influence.
Satan beautifies the people's deeds and bars them from the way, linking deception to wrongful action.
Satan makes people's deeds attractive and turns them from the path, another direct deception-and-action parallel.
Satan made prior nations' deeds attractive and became their patron, explaining a recurring pattern of deluded wrongdoing.
A satanic prompting is met by seeking refuge in God, giving the appropriate response to satanic pressure.
When Satan incites, seeking refuge in God invokes the Hearing, Knowing One, closely contrasting the focus's satanic source.
The prophet seeks refuge from the evil promptings of devils, supplying a direct prophetic counter-response.
He seeks refuge from their presence, extending the preceding protection from satanic intrusion.
Satan sows discord among people, showing destructive influence carried through human speech.
Satan takes hold of people and makes them forget God's remembrance, a related account of corrupted reception.
